content_of_post_to_comment:
I have used no social media except YouTube for years, barely use my phone beyond banking and two-factor authentication. Recently I decided to quit YouTube too. I had given this a shot in the past but wound up back on it. It dawned on me that the easiest way to quit was probably just to shut my laptop and put it away. And I don't want to be overly dramatic about it but that decision has completely changed my life.

Like I said, I don't really use social media and have for a long time considered myself an internet-lite type of guy, but despite what I told myself that wasn't really true. My laptop was often on and I was often sitting in front of it, researching, learning, writing, whatever—cool stuff, but laptop stuff nonetheless.

I also use a laptop for work. My income is dependent on it and I think that's how I ended up using it chronically. Now that I'm trying to manage my usage I'm in this weird space where I open it up, do a days work, and close it again for the rest of the day. What I notice is that the technology has an immediate effect on my internal state.

When I look out the window I see a street, a sky, buildings and a world. And I want to be a part of that world. When I look at the screen I see a different kind of world. And I want that world to wrap around me, to comfort me, because all of a sudden I am anxious and afraid.

Just looking at a screen is enough to make me immediately avoidant.

Just closing the screen is enough to make me want to go outside and breathe sky.

There are things I really wanted to do when I was younger, interests I thought I had grown out of, but now when I look away from the damn laptop long enough I find that I'd still really like to pursue them and I'm wrestling with the realisation that I have not engaged my interests for the bones of a decade because I've been on this damn machine every day.

My twenties are gone.

Don't get me wrong. The stuff I do on a laptop does interest me. What scares me is that these interests—research, learning, investigating—quickly recede when I stop looking at a screen. I can't tell you what the neurology of that is. But a year ago if you could sell me a drug that had the same effect as just shutting my laptop off I would have bought you out.

I'm not saying this is some miracle cure. My sense of it is that I'm going to be reckoning with the effects of this, my addiction or whatever it is, for a very long time. But I feel like, now, I have really seen it, seen what this thing is doing to me.

And I don't like it one bit.
comment: The thing about closing the laptop and suddenly wanting to go outside really rings true. I think there’s a difference between using technology to pursue an interest and letting the environment itself become the place where your brain feels safest. I’ve noticed that boredom after stepping away is often where old interests start coming back.
